page: Vultr vcg-a16-24c-256g-64vram is a dedicated Cloud GPU server designed for memory-intensive parallel processing and graphics-heavy workloads. The system features 24 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel processor running at 2.0 GHz, consisting of 12 physical cores and 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered via four NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs, offering a combined 64 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 1200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in parallel processing and memory operations, though single-core CPU performance is moderate. The server achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1766.38 and a multi-core score of 41473.88, both falling in the average range. Large-block memory bandwidth is measured at 137.58 GB/sec for reads and 56.27 GB/sec for writes. The system excels in LLM inference, achieving top-tier performance in prompt processing with 8464.24 tokens/sec for a 135M model and 614.8 tokens/sec for a 7B model. Text generation speeds are also robust, reaching 32.83 tokens/sec on the 7B model.

This hardware profile offers high resource density, combining substantial system memory with multi-GPU acceleration, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for multi-tenant virtual desktop infrastructure, media streaming, and machine learning inference. However, the 2.0 GHz CPU clock speed presents a tradeoff, as single-threaded tasks like bzip3 decompression perform at average levels. The server is highly suited for LLM inference of small-to-medium models, database operations, parallel data processing, and GPU-accelerated rendering workloads.
